bugs.text: Entry-group delays are compared against the global frame counter, which starts at page load and is never reset per stage, so after the first few seconds every enemy enters at the same instant. The staged fly-in by groups never happens in any real game (screenshot 2: whole formation in place 2.5 s into play).
challenging.waveHits is never incremented, so the 1,000-per-wave and 10,000 PERFECT bonuses can never be awarded and the results screen always reports NUMBER OF HITS 0 and BONUS 0.
A diver that leaves the bottom does not re-enter from the top: startReturn flies it straight back up from its off-bottom position through the playfield to its slot.
Tractor-beam boss stops at y 92-104, inside the Zako rows (y 86/102), so the boss and its red captive sit on top of other enemies and the beam starts inside the formation (screenshot 3).
Capture is instant: the fighter explodes where it is and the captive appears at the boss; there is no pull-up animation into the beam.
Challenging-stage enemies sweep across in a sine wobble rather than looping patterns, and each wave mixes zako/goei/boss sprites.
Wave/perfect bonuses add to score directly instead of addScore, so (were they reachable) they would not update the high score or extra-ship threshold.
READY is only drawn in 'playing' mode; a death during a challenging stage respawns with no READY text.
P does nothing during the STAGE N / result screens; only 'playing' and 'challenging' can be paused.

summary: The file is cleanly organised into state, update and render sections with a hand-rolled 5x5 font, three readable pixel sprites with wing flap, a proper accumulator loop, and every spec feature at least sketched: two-shot limit, extra ships, hit-miss results, boss two-hit colour change, escort-dependent boss scoring, formation sway and breathing, tractor beam with capture, rescue into a working dual fighter, hostile captives, challenging stages, denominated flags, seven synthesized sounds and a mute key. The play-test ran without errors and the screenshots show a recognisable Galaga formation, beam and READY respawn. What keeps it from feeling faithful is the choreography: because entry delays use a never-reset global frame counter the formation materialises in a single 1-2 s rush instead of the arcade's staged fly-ins, divers climb back up from the bottom rather than re-entering from the top, the tractor boss parks inside the Zako rows, capture has no pull-up, and the challenging stage's bonus accounting is dead code since hits are never counted. The core loop is solid and the game is playable from start to game over, but the signature arcade rhythms are only approximated.
